limits: Written against a 2017 pandas (outputs show datetime(2017, 9, 25...)); aliases such as 'M','BM','H','T','A-DEC', resample(kind=, loffset=) and the bare rolling_corr name are version-specific and need checking against the current pandas docs.
Examples use unseeded random data, so printed numbers are not reproducible; stock_px_2.csv and macrodata.csv are book files not described in the chapter.
Timedelta indexes, custom frequency classes and irregular/experimental time are explicitly out of scope.
Typographical faults in the text: In[216]/In[217] are identical; ma60 variable uses window 30 while the prose says 60-day; the convention default is 'start' in prose but 'end' in Table 11-5.
practices: Work in UTC and convert for display, since time zones are the most unpleasant part of time series work (11.4).
Use datetime.strptime for known formats and dateutil.parser.parse / pd.to_datetime for mixed ones; beware parse('42') becomes year 2042 (11.1).
Check index.is_unique and aggregate duplicate timestamps with groupby(level=0) (11.2).
Select ranges by partial date string or slice; slices are views, so edits write through to the original (11.2).
Prefer resample over groupby with offset.rollforward for binning by month (11.3).
Pass freq to shift to move timestamps rather than discard data; use ts / ts.shift(1) - 1 for percent change (11.3).
Use Period/PeriodIndex for fiscal calendars; the same 2012Q4 differs by fiscal year end (11.5).
When downsampling, decide explicitly which side is closed and which edge labels the bin; defaults are arbitrary (11.6 footnote).
For periods, downsampling target must be a subperiod and upsampling target a superperiod, else an exception (11.6).
Use rolling(..., min_periods=n) to avoid NaN at the start, rolling('20D') for irregular series, ewm(span=) for faster adaptation (11.7).

terms.definition: Frequencies that describe points in time that are not evenly spaced, such as 'M' and 'BM', which depend on month length and weekends.
Not a Time, pandas's null value for timestamp data.
A timespan such as a day, month, quarter or year, with a frequency; Period(2007, 'A-DEC') spans Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2007.
Aggregating higher frequency data to lower frequency / converting lower frequency to higher frequency.
Per bucket: first (open), last (close), maximum (high) and minimal (low) values.
Statistics evaluated over a sliding window or with exponentially decaying weights, including functions without a fixed-length window.
